The Institute of Agricultural Sciences (I.Ag.Sc.) at Banaras Hindu University has concluded a distinguished
journey spanning 93 years, marked by substantial contributions towards alleviating hunger in India. Initially
established under various names, it was formally designated as the Institute of Agricultural Sciences in 1981,
with a mission to integrate education, research, extension services, and agricultural development. Pioneering as
the first Institute of Agricultural Research offering M.Sc. and Ph.D. degrees, it commenced undergraduate
education in 1945 under the title of the College of Agriculture within the Faculty of Engineering. This college
attained independent status as the Faculty of Agriculture in 1968.

Presently, the Institute comprises two faculties: the Faculty of Agriculture and the Faculty of Veterinary and
Animal Sciences, encompassing 11 and 15 departments respectively along with three auxiliary units. It currently
provides comprehensive education and involved in research across diverse fields of Agriculture and Veterinary
Sciences, offering programs such as B.Sc. (Ag.), 02 B.Tech. (DT & FT) programs, 11 M.Sc. (Ag.) programs, 02
M.Tech ( DT & FPT) programs, B.V.Sc. & A.H., and Ph.D. programs.

The academic year 2023-24 marked a period of substantial achievement and growth for the institute,
characterized by robust research outputs, strategic collaborations, infrastructure development, and
comprehensive student development initiatives. These accomplishments underscore the commitment of the
Institute to excellence in education, research, and community engagement, positioning it as a leader in
agricultural and allied sciences.

Banaras Hindu University is an internationally reputed temple of learning, situated in the holy city of Varanasi. This creative and innovative university was founded by the great nationalist leader, Pandit Madan Mohan Malaviya, in 1916, through close cooperation with great personalities like Dr Annie Besant, who viewed it as the University of India.
